absent: Locking rules for thread, FPSIMD, vector-length and mitigation state are not shown.
Transition rules for fp_type, SVE/SME enablement and vector-length changes are not shown.
Fault handling, signal delivery and full syscall entry/exit behavior are not shown.
Page-dump walk algorithm and debugfs output format beyond no-op stubs are not shown.
Actual numeric values of TASK_SIZE, DMA limit, SCTLR bits, PSR bits and priority constants beyond their relations are not enumerated here.

findings.text: Context save area holds callee preserved general registers nineteen through twenty eight plus frame pointer stack pointer and program counter. Thread state starts with that context, then a hardened-copy subgroup with two TLS values plus FPMR plus pad plus FPSIMD state, then FP type selector, FPSIMD cpu, optional SVE and SME state pointers, current and exec-time vector lengths, fault address and code, debug info, kernel FPSIMD spill pointer and cpu, and conditional pointer-auth, MTE, SCTLR, SVCR, TPIDR2, POR and guarded-stack fields.

Debug state optionally tracks suspended single-step and whether breakpoints and watchpoints are disabled, plus per-task pinned hardware breakpoint and watchpoint event pointers. Vector kind enumerates SVE then SME with a max sentinel. FP state kind enumerates current-task-based, FPSIMD and SVE selection.

Trap frame is a union of user register view and flat view with thirty one general registers plus stack pointer program counter and saved status, followed by original first argument, syscall number, interrupt priority mask, stolen-time base and a metadata frame record for unwinding.

Page-table dump helpers use an address marker with start and name, dump info with memory descriptor plus markers and base, protection-bit decoding with mask value and set versus clear names, level descriptor with bits name count and mask, and walk state with level, address range where maximum means top of address space, current protection and write-execute plus unprivileged-execute accounting.
Stolen-time ABI record is a packed sixty four byte aligned structure with little-endian revision and attributes plus sixty four bit stolen time and trailing padding.
Low address limit is defined as one below the platform DMA physical limit.

Per-task vector length is stored per vector kind, with separate current and next-exec slots. SVE-specific helpers fix the kind to SVE. Current-length selection prefers SME length when SME is supported and streaming mode is active in SVCR, otherwise SVE length.

User-visible SCTLR mask covers pointer-auth enable bits and memory-tagging control masks. Whitelist helper asserts at build time that the whitelisted thread subgroup has no hidden padding and reports its offset and extent.
User TLS accessor yields the second TLS slot for compatibility threads and the first TLS slot otherwise in one configuration, and unconditionally the first TLS slot in the other configuration.

Thread start for exec zeroes general registers and installs program counter and status, clears saved first argument while preserving syscall number for tracing, installs IRQ-on priority when priority masking is used, and requires a final unwinding frame. Native start uses EL0 thread mode then applies task speculation mitigation and native stack pointer; compatibility start builds 32-bit user status with thumb and endianness adjustments then common start plus mitigation and compatibility stack pointer. New threads default FPSIMD ownership to outside all CPUs.

Speculation mitigation for new execution enables store speculation barrier when global mitigations are off, or when policy is dynamic on a non kernel thread whose SSBD thread flag is clear; the chosen state is written to the status word using the 32-bit or 64-bit SSBS position according to compatibility mode.

An address is treated as TTBR0 when below task size, with tags already cleared by entry code. Kernel task PC and SP inspection read the trap frame program counter and user stack pointer. Prefetch helpers expose load-keep and store-keep L1 hints and advertise their availability.

Vector-length, pointer-auth, tagged-address and timestamp-counter shorthands delegate to underlying current-task or named-task helpers for getting and setting SVE and SME lengths, resetting and enabling pointer-auth keys, and reading or writing tagged-address control and timestamp mode.

Exception level encoding uses one shifted by two for EL1 and two shifted by two for EL2. Initial EL1 status masks debug, async abort, IRQ and FIQ and selects EL1 handler mode. IRQ priority aliases map IRQ-on, IRQ-off and PSR-I-set to architected priority values. Thread-mode and illegal-execution-state bits occupy bit zero and bit twenty.

32-bit status layout defines a five bit mode field with user, FIQ, IRQ, supervisor, abort, hyp, undefined and system encodings, plus thumb, FIQ mask, IRQ mask, async mask, endian, PAN, SSBS, DIT, Q, overflow, carry, zero, negative, If-Then and greater-equal fields. End-state alias is the endian bit on big-endian builds and zero otherwise. Compatibility DIT position differs from the native DIT position.

Compatibility ptrace numbers cover general registers, thread area, syscall, vector registers and hardware breakpoints. Compatibility text, data and text-end addresses and user area size are fixed. Absence of a syscall is represented by negative one.

Compatibility register aliases map indexed slots to user registers including frame pointer, stack pointer, link register, hyp stack pointer, banked IRQ SVC abort undefined and FIQ registers. Conversion between compatibility status and native status moves DIT between its two positions. Register-offset limit ends at saved status and kernel argument extraction covers eight registers.

Syscall presence is decided by comparing syscall number against the no-syscall sentinel, with a helper to clear it. Thumb mode tests the 32-bit thumb bit in one configuration and is constantly false in the other. Processor mode extracts the mode field. User stack selection uses compatibility stack pointer for compatibility mode and native stack pointer otherwise. Indexed register access validates eight byte alignment and returns general registers, stack pointer, program counter, saved status or zero for unknown slots.

Register thirty one behaves as zero register: reads yield zero and writes are ignored. Kernel stack pointer reads the trap-frame stack slot. Return value uses first general register with thirty two bit sign extension for compatibility callers, and setting return value writes that register. Kernel argument fetch returns the indexed register for the first eight arguments and zero beyond. Instruction pointer, frame pointer and link register helpers access program counter, register twenty nine and register thirty.

In this configuration page-dump registration and per-level page callbacks are no-operations. EFI runtime map end aliases the default sixty four bit window. Ring-buffer flush maps to data-cache clean to point of persistence. Realm device name is a fixed identifier string.

Timed conditional load checks elapsed time only after two hundred relaxed polls, otherwise spinning with relaxation. Acquire variant polls with acquire semantics plus wait-for-event hint when the architected timer event stream is available, else falls back to relaxed spinning followed by an acquire barrier. Resource helper instantiates the timed wait with zero elapsed against a unit limit.

Maintainers must keep the whitelisted thread subgroup free of implicit padding, enforced by a build-time size check. Thread start warns if the incoming trap frame does not already present a final frame with zero frame and link records, since unwinding must remain valid throughout.
